title: Staged traffic templates and SIG-driven rollback for pinned model updates
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Objective: Provide a standardized, auditable mechanism for rolling out new model revisions that are pinned by customers, using parameterized traffic templates and statistical-significance-driven (SIG) checkpoints to automatically pause or rollback updates. This ticket scopes the product spec and acceptance criteria for the feature; engineering will implement routing/telemetry hooks and Console will expose template authoring and visibility.

Background: Customers who pin model versions want safe, automated promotion pathways that respect their pin and governance settings. Existing experiments use ad-hoc canaries or shadowing; we need a predictable, reusable flow that balances speed of promotion with signal fidelity.

Key concepts:
- Traffic templates: pre-defined schedules (e.g., 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100%) with configurable hold windows, ramp durations, and cohort weighting. Templates should be parameterized by duration, cohort stratification (region, customer tier), and rollback thresholds.
- SIG checkpoints: After each hold window, run automated checks for regression signals using sequential testing (Bayesian sequential or alpha-spending). Checks include latency regressions, error rate, cost-per-token change, and quality regressions from a small evaluation prompt set.
- Pinned-aware semantics: When a customer pins a route to a model family, the template must operate on a pinned revision namespace and respect customer-level guardrails (no forced promotion without owner approval).

Success metrics:
- 75% of internal canary promotions use a traffic template on first pass within 8 weeks of launch.
- Mean time to detect regression during rollout reduced by 40%.
- Automated rollback accuracy (true rollback where regressions exist) > 90% on historic replay tests.

Scope & deliverables:
1) Product spec: UI flow for selecting a traffic template when creating a pinned revision rollout; audit trail showing checkpoints and decision log.
2) Backend routing: support for templated traffic slices and cohort routing rules that can be attached to a pinned revision.
3) Telemetry & eval: label traffic slices in telemetry, add a small canonical eval set per model onboarding to feed SIG checks, and surface per-slice metrics in Console.
4) Automation: server-side SIG engine that evaluates sequential tests and emits decisions (continue, hold, rollback, manual-review-needed).
5) Console: template library, one-click start, live view of checkpoint decisions, and rollback button.

Signals and thresholds (initial proposal):
- Latency p95 increase > 15% relative to baseline -> fail checkpoint.
- Error rate increase (client error + server error) > 0.5 percentage points -> fail.
- Cost per 1k tokens increase > 20% without commensurate quality gain -> flag for manual review.
- Quality regression: drop in quality score on canonical eval prompts by more than 3% absolute (or posterior probability in Bayesian test > 0.95) -> fail.

Acceptance criteria:
- Product: Console has a Traffic Templates page with at least three built-in templates and the ability to create a custom template; audit log entry for each checkpoint produced.
- Backend: Requests can be routed per-template slice and slices are labeled in metrics with slice_id and template_id.
- SIG engine: Runs sequential checks automatically at each hold window and records decision + rationale.
- Safety: Rollback path re-applies previous pinned revision weighting within 30s of a decision to rollback.
- Docs: PRD and runbook published with sample templates and troubleshooting guide.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Statistical method: prefer Bayesian sequential analysis for faster detection, but need to validate calibration vs historic traffic patterns.
- Evaluation set size: smaller eval sets detect quality regressions faster but increase variance; propose a mixed approach combining production hold-slice feedback with a curated eval set.
- Customer control: how much override should be allowed for enterprise tenants (e.g., force-promote even when SIG flags)? propose an explicit enterprise override with audit and a required post-mortem.

Artifacts & links:
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Templated+Pin+Rollouts
- Design mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rollout-templates-ui
- Telemetry schema proposal: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/214

Rollout plan: Pilot with internal teams and 3 beta customers, collect replay-based validation against historical canary runs, iterate thresholds and priors, then enable self-serve in Console as opt-in for 2 quarters before defaulting templates for new pins.
